title: The Centurion's Faith and Forgiveness

questions.question: When Jesus entered Capernaum, a centurion had a servant who was sick and at the point of death. Who did the centurion send to ask Jesus to heal his servant?
options: Elders of the Jews
Some Roman soldiers
His own wife
The servant's mother
questions.explanation: Luke 7:3 (ESV): "When the centurion heard about Jesus, he sent to him elders of the Jews, asking him to come and heal his servant."

questions.question: What reason did the Jewish elders give Jesus as to why the centurion was worthy to have this done for him?
options: "He loves our nation, and he is the one who built us our synagogue."
"He is a very wealthy and generous man."
"He freed many of our Jewish slaves."
"He secretly converted to our religion and obeys the law."
questions.correctAnswer: "He loves our nation, and he is the one who built us our synagogue."
questions.explanation: Luke 7:5 (ESV): "for he loves our nation, and he is the one who built us our synagogue."

questions.question: When Jesus was not far from the house, the centurion sent friends to say, "Lord, do not trouble yourself, for I am not worthy to have you come under my roof." Instead, what did he believe Jesus needed to do?
options: "But say the word, and let my servant be healed."
"Send an angel to touch him."
"Tell me what medicine to buy."
"Pray to your Father continuously."
questions.correctAnswer: "But say the word, and let my servant be healed."
questions.explanation: Luke 7:7 (ESV): "Therefore I did not presume to come to you. But say the word, and let my servant be healed."

questions.question: Why did Jesus marvel at the centurion?
options: Because of his great faith; "not even in Israel have I found such faith."
Because a Roman cared so deeply for his servant
Because he was so rich yet so humble
Because he sent Jewish elders instead of commanding it
questions.correctAnswer: Because of his great faith; "not even in Israel have I found such faith."
questions.explanation: Luke 7:9 (ESV): "When Jesus heard these things, he marveled at him, and turning to the crowd... said, 'I tell you, not even in Israel have I found such faith.'"

questions.question: Jesus went to a town called Nain. As he drew near the gate of the town, what did He encounter?
options: A man who had died was being carried out, the only son of his mother, and she was a widow
A leper banished from the city screaming for healing
A crowd throwing stones at a tax collector
A massive feast welcoming the governor
questions.correctAnswer: A man who had died was being carried out, the only son of his mother, and she was a widow
questions.explanation: Luke 7:12 (ESV): "As he drew near to the gate of the town, behold, a man who had died was being carried out, the only son of his mother, and she was a widow..."

questions.question: Having compassion on the widow, Jesus touched the bier and commanded the dead man: "Young man, I say to you, arise." What did the dead man do immediately?
options: The dead man sat up and began to speak, and Jesus gave him to his mother
The dead man arose completely whole and ran into the city
The dead man's eyes opened, and he was healed of leprosy
He sighed deeply, but did not awake entirely until later
questions.correctAnswer: The dead man sat up and began to speak, and Jesus gave him to his mother
questions.explanation: Luke 7:15 (ESV): "And the dead man sat up and began to speak, and Jesus gave him to his mother."

questions.question: When John the Baptist's disciples reported all these things to him, John sent two disciples to ask Jesus what?
options: "Are you the one who is to come, or shall we look for another?"
"When will you overthrow Herod and set me free?"
"Have you forgotten my cousin in his chains?"
"Should we fast until the day of judgment?"
questions.correctAnswer: "Are you the one who is to come, or shall we look for another?"
questions.explanation: Luke 7:19 (ESV): "and sent them to the Lord, saying, 'Are you the one who is to come, or shall we look for another?'"

questions.question: Jesus told John's disciples to report what they had seen and heard: the blind see, the lame walk, lepers are cleansed, the deaf hear, the dead are raised, and the poor have good news preached to them. What did He add?
options: "And blessed is the one who is not offended by me."
"And cursed are those who put John in prison."
"And tell John his reward will be great."
"And blessed are all those who fast in the desert."
questions.correctAnswer: "And blessed is the one who is not offended by me."
questions.explanation: Luke 7:23 (ESV): "And blessed is the one who is not offended by me."

questions.question: Jesus asked the crowds what they went out into the wilderness to see. Did they go to see a man dressed in soft clothing?
options: No, for those in splendid clothing and living in luxury are in kings' courts
Yes, for John wore the fine robes of a priest
No, for John wore armor like a soldier
Yes, many went to see the soft clothing of the elite in the desert
questions.correctAnswer: No, for those in splendid clothing and living in luxury are in kings' courts
questions.explanation: Luke 7:25 (ESV): "What then did you go out to see? A man dressed in soft clothing? Behold, those who are dressed in splendid clothing and live in luxury are in kings' courts."

questions.question: What did Jesus say about John the Baptist's greatness compared to those born of women?
options: "Among those born of women none is greater than John. Yet the one who is least in the kingdom of God is greater than he."
"He is exactly equal to Elijah and Moses combined."
"There is no one holier in the world than John in prison right now."
"He is simply a messenger preparing the true path."
questions.correctAnswer: "Among those born of women none is greater than John. Yet the one who is least in the kingdom of God is greater than he."
questions.explanation: Luke 7:28 (ESV): "I tell you, among those born of women none is greater than John. Yet the one who is least in the kingdom of God is greater than he."

questions.question: A Pharisee invited Jesus to eat with him. A woman of the city, a sinner, learned He was there and brought an alabaster flask of ointment. What did she do behind Jesus at His feet?
options: She washed his feet with her tears, wiped them with her hair, kissed them, and anointed them with ointment
She poured the ointment entirely out on the table before Him
She rubbed the ointment into His hands and begged forgiveness
She merely stood weeping, not touching Him because she was unclean
questions.correctAnswer: She washed his feet with her tears, wiped them with her hair, kissed them, and anointed them with ointment
questions.explanation: Luke 7:37-38 (ESV): "and standing behind him at his feet, weeping, she began to wet his feet with her tears and wiped them with the hair of her head and kissed his feet and anointed them with the ointment."

questions.question: The Pharisee Simon said to himself, "If this man were a prophet, he would have known who and what sort of woman this is who is touching him." How did Jesus respond?
options: He told a parable about a moneylender who canceled the debts of two debtors, one owing 500 denarii and the other 50
He pointed out that Simon was a far worse sinner in secret
He ordered the woman out to please Simon
He miraculously proved He knew Simon's full genealogy
questions.correctAnswer: He told a parable about a moneylender who canceled the debts of two debtors, one owing 500 denarii and the other 50
questions.explanation: Luke 7:41-42 (ESV): "A certain moneylender had two debtors. One owed five hundred denarii, and the other fifty. When they could not pay, he canceled the debt of both..."

questions.question: In the parable, which debtor will love the moneylender more?
options: The one for whom he canceled the larger debt
The one who owed fifty, for he appreciated the gesture
Both equally, for they are debt-free
Neither owed him thanks, for charging interest is wrong
questions.correctAnswer: The one for whom he canceled the larger debt
questions.explanation: Luke 7:42-43 (ESV): "'Now which of them will love him more?' Simon answered, 'The one, I suppose, for whom he canceled the larger debt.'"

questions.question: What did Jesus say to Simon about what Simon had failed to provide when Jesus entered his house, unlike the woman?
options: Water for his feet, a kiss of greeting, and oil for his head
A fine cut of roasted lamb for dinner
A proper introduction to the other guests
A donation to the poor before sitting to eat
questions.correctAnswer: Water for his feet, a kiss of greeting, and oil for his head
questions.explanation: Luke 7:44-46 (ESV): "...You gave me no water for my feet... You gave me no kiss... You did not anoint my head with oil, but she has anointed my feet with ointment."

questions.question: Jesus declared to the woman "Your sins are forgiven," and finally said what to her before she departed?
options: "Your faith has saved you; go in peace."
"Do not sin anymore, lest something worse happen."
"Tell no one what occurred here today."
"Go and give half your belongings to the poor."
questions.correctAnswer: "Your faith has saved you; go in peace."
questions.explanation: Luke 7:50 (ESV): "And he said to the woman, 'Your faith has saved you; go in peace.'"

key_verse_text: And he said to the woman, "Your faith has saved you; go in peace."
